note: Fixed Block Content provides a fixed_block_content config entity (keys id, title, block_content_bundle, default_content, auto_export, protected) that wraps a custom block_content so a placement never breaks. A derived block plugin fixed_block_content:<id> is placeable. Configure route entity.fixed_block_content.collection (/admin/structure/block-content/fixed-block-content), gated by core permission 'administer block types'; depends on block_content + hal; no own permissions, Drush, or plugin types. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real fixed_block_content config entities (fbc_known/fbc_prot/fbc_task/fbc_ptask) targeting the existing 'basic' block_content bundle, created and torn down by the scripts (cleanup also deletes any block_content the entity lazily created).

evals.prompt: What problem does the Drupal fixed_block_content module solve, and how does it stop a placed custom block from showing 'This block is broken or missing'?
evals.expected_output: It wraps a custom (block_content) block in a fixed_block_content configuration entity referenced by a stable machine name, so the placement is config (deployed with the site) and always resolves; if the underlying custom block is missing/deleted it recreates an empty one on demand instead of rendering a broken block.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with fixed_block_content enabled, where do I create and manage fixed blocks, what config entity type is used, and what permission is required?
evals.expected_output: Manage them at Structure -> Block content -> Fixed block content (/admin/structure/block-content/fixed-block-content, route entity.fixed_block_content.collection). They are 'fixed_block_content' config entities. Access requires the core 'administer block types' permission.

evals.prompt: After I create a fixed block with fixed_block_content, what block plugin do I place in Block layout, and under which block category does it appear?
evals.expected_output: A derived block plugin with id fixed_block_content:<fixed_block_id> is created for each fixed block and appears under the 'Fixed custom' category in Block layout; you can also choose the view mode it renders the custom block in.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a fixed_block_content entity titled 'Known Footer Block'. Inspect the live configuration and tell me which custom block type (block_content bundle) it wraps.
evals.expected_output: It wraps the 'basic' custom block type: fixed_block_content.fixed_block_content.fbc_known has block_content_bundle: basic.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a fixed_block_content entity with machine id 'fbc_prot'. Inspect its live configuration: is its custom block protected (marked non-reusable) or not?
evals.expected_output: Yes, it is protected: fixed_block_content.fixed_block_content.fbc_prot has protected: true, so its custom block is marked non-reusable.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the fixed_block_content module to create a fixed block with machine id 'fbc_task' and title 'Task Block' that wraps a custom block of the 'basic' block type. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create and save a fixed_block_content config entity with id fbc_task and block_content_bundle 'basic' (via the fixed_block_content storage or the add form at /admin/structure/block-content/fixed-block-content/add). Verify checks the entity exists with block_content_bundle basic.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a fixed_block_content entity 'fbc_ptask'. Using fixed_block_content, mark its custom block as protected (non-reusable) so it cannot be edited or deleted independently. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set protected to TRUE on fixed_block_content.fixed_block_content.fbc_ptask (e.g. $entity->setProtected(TRUE)->save()). Verify checks isProtected() === TRUE.
